claim: One month into DMA choice-screen enforcement (April 2024), Mozilla itself estimated fewer than one-fifth of iOS users and likely fewer Android users had even been shown a choice screen, meaning the natural experiment's exposure was still minimal at that stage.
stance_target: measurement window and exposure denominator for switching claims
scope_conditions: EU iOS/Android, April 2024, one month post 7 March 2024 compliance deadline
quoted_support: Mozilla... told us it estimates that less than a fifth of iOS users have been shown a choice screen so far. It reckons even fewer Android users have seen one in the wild as yet.
numbers: <20% of iOS users exposed as of April 2024

claim: Opera's iOS EU new-user growth rate decelerated from an initial +164% spike (as of 18 March 2024) to +63% (Feb-end March) and +39% (default-browser selections, 3 March-4 April), indicating an early spike followed by decay rather than sustained acceleration.
stance_target: choice-screen-driven switching is persistent and growing, not a decaying novelty effect
scope_conditions: EU iOS, March-April 2024, self-reported by Opera, no independent audit
quoted_support: Previously (as of March 18), Opera reported 164% growth in the inflow of new EU users on iOS after the deadline for Apple to implement the DMA-enforced choice screen. So there actually appears to have been a drop in the growth rate it's seen over this period.

claim: Yandex reported no meaningful change in user metrics in the EU region despite appearing on the iOS choice screen, a genuine null result among the browsers surveyed, plausibly confounded by anti-Russia sentiment post-Ukraine invasion rather than choice-screen design.
stance_target: mandated choice screens universally and reliably produce switching
quoted_support: Yandex, a Russia-based browser that can appear on the iOS choice screen anywhere in the EU, told us it hasn't seen "any meaningful changes in the user metrics in the region so far."

claim: Ecosia and other smaller browsers attributed muted choice-screen gains to specific Apple design flaws: the screen appearing even to users who already chose an alternative, and Safari retaining the best home-screen position, alongside a complex install flow that 'loses a large number of users.'
stance_target: whether current choice-screen design fully tests the inertia-vs-preference hypothesis, or is confounded by implementation friction
scope_conditions: EU iOS choice screen design, April 2024
quoted_support: such as showing the choice screen to users who have already selected an alternative choice to Safari; an overly complex installation process which loses a large number of users; and keeping the Safari browser app in the best position on the home screen.

claim: Self-reported early browser growth figures (Aloha +250%, Vivaldi +36.7% to +69.6% in choice-screen markets, Brave daily iOS installs roughly doubling) are all relative percentage gains off very small absolute bases (e.g., Aloha estimates only ~1 million of its 10 million global MAU are in the EU) and are unaudited by any independent party or the European Commission, which explicitly declined to share its own tracking data.
scope_conditions: EU iOS/Android, March-April 2024, self-reported, no EC or third-party verification
quoted_support: We also contacted the European Commission to ask about its own tracking of the DMA's impact in this area — but it declined to share any data.
numbers: Aloha +250% new users, ~1M of 10M MAU estimated EU-based
Vivaldi +36.7% EU-wide downloads, +69.6% in its 8 choice-screen markets
Brave iOS EU daily installs ~7,500 to 11,000-14,000
